title: Border and Drop
premise: Ada Reyes, a forensic accountant who launders the reputations of dirty money, is handed the one case her firm wants buried: Flight 4072, a charter whose passenger manifest, flight plan, and radar trail have been erased mid-flight. Following the money instead of the plane, she uncovers a laundering pipeline run by the very agency that regulates her — and discovers her own estranged brother piloted the vanished flight. To expose it she must surrender the one secret she's kept for a decade: the ledger proving she once laundered money for a cartel to buy her brother's freedom from them. In the end, Ada trades her secret to a federal prosecutor, burning her career and nearly her life, but the pipeline collapses, her brother walks out of the wreckage alive, and the found family she built among the investigation's outcasts becomes the only clean thing she has left.
about_author: Xanthe Underhill is a former compliance analyst who spent eight years tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a coastal town she refuses to name, where she keeps a wall of index cards connected by red string that her neighbors assume is art.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She scrubs a corrupt senator's finances into respectability, revealing the moral rot beneath her lucrative work. Her handler, Marsh, warns her to stay shallow. Emotional beat: competent numbness cracking into quiet self-disgust.

chapters.title: The Case No One Wants
chapters.summary: Marsh slides her the 4072 file — a charter flight whose records vanished while airborne. Every agency has declined it. Ada notices the erasure was too clean, done with regulator-grade credentials. Emotional beat: the thrill of a puzzle she knows she shouldn't touch.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes of Silence
chapters.summary: Ada reconstructs the flight's last forty minutes from fuel purchases and catering invoices. The plane never filed a destination. POV alternates with a brief, unnamed pilot logging a mayday that no tower received. Emotional beat: dread arriving through arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Man Who Pays in Cash
chapters.summary: Ada tracks the charter's owner to a marina bar and meets Dez, a disgraced air-traffic controller feeding her clues for reasons he won't share. First sparks of wary alliance. Emotional beat: loneliness recognizing loneliness.

chapters.title: Shell Game
chapters.summary: A layer-cake of shell companies points to Meridian Compliance Group — the regulator that licenses Ada's own firm. She realizes the fox audits the henhouse. Emotional beat: vertigo as the safe world tilts.

chapters.title: What the Brother Knew
chapters.summary: Ada's POV turns inward: her estranged brother Tomas went quiet three weeks ago. A fuel receipt places him near the charter hangar. Emotional beat: fear she can't separate from love.

chapters.title: Marsh's Warning
chapters.summary: Marsh tells her to drop 4072, then offers her a promotion to make her drop it. Ada understands the bribe is a leash. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of being managed.

chapters.title: Dez's Confession
chapters.summary: Dez admits he was on duty the night 4072 vanished and was ordered to log it as never having taken off. He kept a fragment of the radar tape. Emotional beat: guilt finding a purpose.

chapters.title: The Hangar at Night
chapters.summary: Ada breaks into the charter hangar and finds the plane — intact, re-registered, repainted. Someone needed 4072 to disappear, not to crash. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration in equal measure.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Following the re-registration, Ada finds a pattern: eleven flights erased over six years, all carrying people, not cargo. Extraction or trafficking — she can't yet tell. Emotional beat: the weight of faces she'll never see.

chapters.title: Tomas Calls
chapters.summary: A burner call: Tomas is alive, terrified, and tells her to stop digging. In the background, a voice she half-recognizes — Marsh's cadence. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of her loyalties.

chapters.title: The Cartel Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: ten years ago, Ada laundered cartel money to buy Tomas out of their employ, keeping the ledger as insurance ever since. Emotional beat: the secret's origin, and its cost.

chapters.title: Someone in Her Apartment
chapters.summary: Ada returns to find her files photographed, nothing taken. A message scrawled in her notebook: WE KNOW ABOUT 2014. Emotional beat: violation, and the secret becoming a countdown.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Ada, Dez, and Priya — a Meridian whistleblower Ada recruits — form a fragile triangle in a diner booth, pooling what they know. Emotional beat: the first warmth of found family, and the fear of what that will cost them.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Name
chapters.summary: Priya identifies a passenger on 4072: a Meridian auditor who'd found the pipeline and was being flown out — extracted by the good guys, or disappeared by the bad. Emotional beat: moral ambiguity sharpening into a blade.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Ada realizes she's being followed through the city and runs a counter-surveillance route Dez taught her, losing the tail in a rail yard. Emotional beat: fear metabolized into competence.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs
chapters.summary: Priya is suspended and threatened with prosecution for the leak; she wavers about staying in. Ada argues for the truth; Priya argues for her pension and her kids. Emotional beat: love against duty, both sides right.

chapters.title: The Broker
chapters.summary: Ada meets the pipeline's broker, Voss, who offers her a job instead of a bullet — her laundering talent, weaponized. He shows her Tomas's debt ledger as leverage. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: Refusal, First Draft
chapters.summary: Ada pretends to consider Voss's offer to buy time, feeding him a false version of her investigation while Dez copies the radar fragment. Emotional beat: the intoxication and shame of playing double.

chapters.title: Radar Fragment
chapters.summary: The fragment shows 4072 landing at a decommissioned airstrip — inside a Meridian-chartered 'conservation zone.' People went in. Nothing came out. Emotional beat: the case turning from financial to human.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Priya, cornered by Meridian, chooses the family they've become over her career and hands Ada internal routing codes. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given, and its terror.

chapters.title: Into the Zone
chapters.summary: Ada and Dez infiltrate the airstrip at night: barracks, a medical wing, and a manifest of the disappeared — witnesses, whistleblowers, inconvenient people, held not killed. Emotional beat: horror that is almost worse than corpses.

chapters.title: Tomas, Found
chapters.summary: Ada finds Tomas among the detained — he was the pilot who refused to fly the twelfth extraction. Their reunion is interrupted by patrol sweepers. Emotional beat: love arriving too late to be simple.

chapters.title: The Runway
chapters.summary: A chase across the airstrip; Dez is captured covering their escape. Ada and Tomas get out with photographs of the manifest. Emotional beat: survival purchased with someone else's freedom.

chapters.title: The Trade Proposed
chapters.summary: Voss contacts Ada: Dez for the radar fragment and her silence. Meanwhile a federal prosecutor, Okafor, has been circling Ada's own 2014 ledger. Emotional beat: two doors, both leading through her secret.

chapters.title: Okafor's Offer
chapters.summary: Prosecutor Okafor reveals she has the 2014 ledger already — Voss sold her a copy — and offers Ada immunity in exchange for testimony that would take months Ada doesn't have. Emotional beat: the trap closing from the legal side too.

chapters.title: Dez, Interrogated
chapters.summary: Dez's POV in captivity: he stalls Voss's men by feeding them the false timeline Ada planted, protecting her without knowing if she's coming. Emotional beat: faith as a form of resistance.

chapters.title: The Secret's Price
chapters.summary: Ada weighs it: trade the ledger to Voss for Dez, or give it to Okafor and lose the time. Tomas begs her to run with him instead. Emotional beat: every love asking for a different sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada and Priya attempt to forge a plausible fake of the 2014 ledger to buy Dez's release — but Ada's own conscience rebels at laundering even her own past. Emotional beat: the forger refusing to forge.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Voss moves the exchange up twelve hours; simultaneously Okafor's grand jury convenes. Ada must choose in a single night. Emotional beat: time as antagonist.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Ada gives Voss the real ledger — and a beacon hidden inside its encryption, courtesy of Dez's old ATC equipment, traded for Dez's release. Emotional beat: paying the price and rigging the scale.

chapters.title: Dez Comes Home
chapters.summary: Dez, freed and broken-footed, insists on finishing it. The team plans to hit the airstrip the same night Okafor's warrants land. Emotional beat: the found family choosing its shape.

chapters.title: Warrants at Dawn
chapters.summary: Okafor's raids begin across Meridian — but Voss, tipped off, begins moving detainees to a final flight. The twelfth extraction is happening now. Emotional beat: the race becoming real.

chapters.title: Flight 4072, Again
chapters.summary: Ada and Tomas reach the airstrip as detainees are loaded onto a re-registered 4072. Ada makes the call Okafor forbade: she broadcasts the manifest on every open channel. Emotional beat: duty redefined on her own terms.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Public exposure freezes the flight; Voss's men scatter; Okafor's agents arrive to a scene Ada has already lit up. Voss corners Ada on the tarmac. Emotional beat: the confrontation she's been flying toward all book.

chapters.title: The Tarmac
chapters.summary: Voss offers Ada everything — her record cleaned, Tomas freed, Dez safe — for the beacon's off switch. She refuses, and Tomas's testimony puts Voss down. Emotional beat: love against duty, and love winning by refusing the trade.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ada testifies, surrendering the real ledger publicly — her cartel past, her bargains, all of it. The immunity holds; her career does not. Emotional beat: the price paid in full, and strangely light.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Meridian collapses; the detained are released; Dez testifies about the night 4072 vanished and is reinstated. Marsh resigns rather than face Okafor. Emotional beat: justice as repair, not triumph.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Ada, unlicensed and unemployable in finance, opens a small forensic bookkeeping practice for victims of fraud. Tomas rebuilds his life; Priya visits with her kids. Emotional beat: the quiet after the storm, and its unexpected warmth.

chapters.title: Border and Drop
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ada's POV: she and Dez fly a small rented plane along the old route, finally logging 4072's true flight path in a memorial archive. The border between her old life and new one is the drop she chose to make. Emotional beat: peace earned, love chosen, the ledger finally closed.
